flags.name: --location
flags.description: Engine location, cloud or local; separate from agent location.

flags.name: --state-dir
flags.description: Explicit absolute owner-only OpenWiz state directory.

flags.name: --operation
flags.description: Exact 32-hex setup operation returned by engine preview.

flags.name: --root
flags.description: The verified installation root created by install.py --root; Local engine activation only.

flags.name: --help
flags.description: Print human help without sources or state; only for commands listing this flag.

flags.name: --agent
flags.description: Print this machine catalogue; only help --agent.

flags.name: --json
flags.description: Select the declared JSON success report instead of human text.

flags.name: -l
flags.description: Read reported configuration for sessions on the page; combinable with -a.

flags.name: -a
flags.description: Include archived sessions; combinable with -l.

flags.name: --hidden
flags.description: Include hidden sessions.

flags.name: --limit
flags.description: Whole number of rows, 0 through 200.

flags.name: --offset
flags.description: Whole number of matched sessions to skip.

flags.name: --steer
flags.description: Request Steer; otherwise Queue. Never automatic mode selection or fallback.

flags.name: --op-id
flags.default: generated for send/new; required for send.check
flags.description: 1–64 ASCII letters/digits/_/-, starting with a letter or digit; binds one attempt.

flags.name: --resume-paused-queue
flags.description: Explicitly acknowledge resuming a paused or possibly paused queue.

flags.name: --accept-possible-duplicate
flags.description: Explicitly acknowledge an uncertain/in-progress earlier matching send under another op id.

flags.name: --attach
flags.description: Stage this path first; /bin/df measures free space. A failed path reports every path and prevents CloudRoom reads and send/create.

flags.name: --attachment
flags.description: Use a ready staged attachment id, preserving combined attachment-flag order; IDs in the combined list must be unique.

flags.name: --preview
flags.description: Read send effects without claiming, sending, or opening the send record.

flags.name: --check
flags.description: Read the send record only; no source call or claim.

flags.name: --project-id
flags.description: Use an exact existing project id instead of the positional display name.

flags.name: --harness
flags.description: Required offered Cloud harness; no default or substitution.

flags.name: --model
flags.description: Required offered model for the harness; no default or substitution.

flags.name: --effort
flags.description: Required offered effort; no default or substitution.

flags.name: --text-sha256
flags.description: 64 lowercase hex SHA-256 digits; refuse if prompt bytes differ.

flags.name: --yes
flags.description: Create one Cloud thread; absent means preview only.

flags.name: --status
flags.description: Read one new-thread operation by op id; no create options, project or text.
End option parsing. Remaining operands, including flag-looking strings, are data.

flags.name: --dry-run
flags.description: Read and plan fleet actions only: no locks, writes, starts or messages.

flags.name: --expect-plan
flags.description: Require a reviewed fleet tick dry-run JSON file; refuse before effects on pending recovery or any changed ordered action, rule or default branch.

flags.name: --github-only
flags.description: Read-only GitHub candidate check; required for fleet due, with no CloudRoom or state access.

flags.name: --port
flags.description: The running local openwiz-server's port on 127.0.0.1: one decimal number, 1 to 65535.

flags.name: --repository
flags.description: Required GitHub repository OWNER/NAME whose App installation mints the token.

flags.name: --read
flags.description: Ask for exactly the read-only permission profile.

flags.name: --allowed-host
flags.description: The server's configured public DNS host name for guarded requests (no scheme, path, port, IP or loopback name); otherwise OPENWIZ_SERVER_ALLOWED_HOST; absent means reads only.

results.when: handled error with syntactic --json and no existing outcome report

exits.meaning: Result printed or quiet when nothing needs reporting; inspect per-action outcomes.
Required read, planning, setup or output failed, or the reviewed plan was unreadable, invalid, mismatched or could not authorize pending recovery.

rules: No positional operands; options occur once, with no =value or -- delimiter. --expect-plan consumes one nonempty UTF-8 path token, even when flag-like, and is execution-only (never --dry-run or due).
Default-branch fleet rules and current plan approvals gate every action; unknown facts fail closed.
Without --dry-run, execute approved actions: start builders/reviewers, send findings, merge/close/hold/archive and record or notify judgment items through existing allowlisted adapters.
OPENWIZ_ORCHESTRATOR_THREAD_ID supplies the verified Needs you destination; absent or unverified targets leave notifications due.
Human output includes wake/Needs you items and one line for every refused, failed or uncertain action; JSON reports all actions/outcomes. Exit 0 does not mean every action succeeded.

With --expect-plan PATH, require the strict complete dry_run envelope: exact ordered actions, arguments, planned outcomes, rules and default branch; validate planned_at only. Pending recovery or any mismatch refuses before external or local writes. Existing authority gates still apply; absent means existing behavior.

commands.name: github.token

exits.meaning: Token printed on stdout alone; its expiry on stderr.
App key or App id missing or unusable, no complete answer from GitHub, or output failure; no token.
Usage error; nothing read or minted.
No installation of this App covers the repository.
Refused: GitHub refused, or the answer granted other permissions or repositories or failed the expiry guards.

rules: Reads the key only from OPENWIZ_GITHUB_APP_KEY and the App id from OPENWIZ_GITHUB_APP_ID; authenticates as an installation, never as an App user.
Without --read exactly the App's profile; with --read exactly the read profile, for exactly that one repository.
Stores nothing: each call mints a fresh token of at most about an hour. The key and token never reach an argument, URL, log or error.
Plain text only: no --json form; stderr is one fixed sentence on failure.

notes: Only shipped dispatch forms are listed, including fleet tick/due and the visual terminal entry (ui, and interactive no-argument openwiz).
Help forms read no sources and write no state; syntactic --json wraps recognized human help, including loop-only help.
Syntactic JSON selects exactly one declared success, outcome, help or error document. Existing report shapes and numeric exit meanings are unchanged; a nonzero report remains a report.
Explicit commands remain noninteractive. Only ui, or no arguments with a terminal on stdin and stdout, opens the terminal app; no command starts a service.
Value operands and text after -- are data, never JSON selection. Existing success reports/exit meanings are preserved.
Broken stdout cannot carry a JSON error document; see the separate output-failure limitation in contracts/cli.v1.md.
Fixture proof establishes no live behaviour.
